ranking.rationale: Trip distance is the most semantically stable predictor of taxi outcomes and should generalize across domains better than time-of-day or calendar features, which are more prone to shift and shortcut effects.

Direction is a stable trip-level signal that can complement distance by capturing route geometry and destination orientation, which should generalize better across domains than calendar/time features that are more likely to reflect domain-specific temporal shifts or shortcuts.
Hour of day is a stable, semantically meaningful demand signal for taxi trips and complements distance/direction without strongly encoding domain-specific artifacts.

Minute-of-day adds finer-grained temporal signal beyond hour and is likely to remain semantically predictive for taxi demand patterns across domains, while month/week/weekday are coarser and more prone to capturing dataset-specific seasonal or split artifacts.

Day-of-week can capture stable weekly demand patterns and operational differences that often generalize better than month or week-of-year, while adding less brittle seasonal or dataset-specific drift beyond the already selected time-of-day and trip geometry features.

Week of year can capture recurring seasonal demand patterns that are more stable and fine-grained than month, while still being less likely to act as a brittle domain identifier once distance, direction, and time-of-day features are already included.

Month can capture broad seasonal demand and traffic patterns that are likely to remain predictive across splits, while adding less brittle, domain-specific information than finer-grained temporal features already selected.
